text:
Maya: 03:10 UTC alert — high GPU mem and throttling on us-east-1 during batch rerank. Observed near-OOM (98% mem on GPU0), latency p95 jumped x4, throughput fell ~35%. Putting notes here for post-analysis.

oncall-bot: ALERT @channel: inference-cluster-us-east1 GPU memory high (98%), pods throttled, incident created INC-2026-032.

Liam: can you paste the short metrics? p50/p95 latency, GPU mem over time, and which model variant was used?

Maya: p50 stayed ~120ms, p95 went 520ms -> 2.2s during the spike. Throughput 1400 reqs/s -> 900 reqs/s. Model: rdx-13b-qa (quantized q4_0), batch_size=16, KV cache warmed.

Sophia: initial guess: KV cache growth + large batch_size triggered memory pressure. Also autoscaler didn't add nodes because we hit daemonset pod density limits on p4d racks. Suggest immediate mitigations: reduce batch_size to 8, enable per-tenant priority-based eviction, fall back to rdx-7b for burst traffic.

Raj: capacity note — our forecast for this week underestimated routing churn from a new partner by ~22%. Current committed GPUs: 120 p4d-equivalents. Peak observed demand this incident ~150 equivalent. We should plan for +25% buffer for the next 90 days.

Olivia: cost tradeoff: adding 30 reserved p4d equivalents increases monthly commit by ~$85k. Short-term we can use spot + burst from dedicated pool, but need SLA for partner traffic. I'll run cost vs SLA scenarios.

Liam: ops checklist I ran:
```
kubectl top pods -n inference
# NAME             CPU(cores)   MEMORY(bytes)
inference-abc      1100m        62000Mi
inference-xyz      980m         59000Mi
```
Also saw kernel logs with repeated allocation failures before throttling.

Maya: quick mitigation applied at 03:25: reduced batch_size -> 8, activated fallback route to rdx-7b for non-critical queues. Memory usage dropped to ~72% within 3 minutes, throughput recovered to ~95% of pre-spike.

Sophia: learned items: 1) Autoscaler policy thresholds (scaleUp when node mem > 70%) are too late for large model cold-starts. 2) We need density-aware scheduling — avoid packing many heavy pods on same p4d rack. 3) Add a soft per-tenant memory guard and early fallback to smaller model.

Raj: forecasting update actions: I'll add a ramp model for partner on-boarding +20% demand, request +40 GPUs in us-east-1 for next quarter, and propose a seasonal buffer of +15% for holiday spikes.

Olivia: action: I'll compare reserved vs on-demand vs spot mix and share 3 scenarios by EOD. If we need quick capacity, recommend converting 10 on-demand to reserved for 6 months to get price stability.

Liam: I'll add a new dashboard tile: GPU mem headroom heatmap, rack-level pod density, and an alert when inferred fallback rate > 5%. Also update autoscaler to consider pod memory growth rate not just absolute mem.

Maya: postmortem notes: root cause = KV cache growth + oversized batch on high-density racks + autoscaler thresholds tuned for CPU not memory. Immediate fixes applied. Follow-ups: Raj: capacity request; Olivia: cost scenarios; Liam: dashboards + autoscaler tweak; Sophia: implement per-tenant guard and fallback policy.

Sophia: small config snippet for fallback backoff I recommend:
```
--fallback-backoff-ms=200
--tenant-memory-guard=0.75
```
Test in staging before rollout.

Maya: thanks everyone. Marking INC-2026-032 as "mitigated". We'll collect model traces and KV cache histograms and reconvene tomorrow for the full RCA. :eyes:
